simple.meaning: דָּגָה (dâgâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “fish.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 15 times across Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Psalms, and 3 more, beginning at Genesis 1:26. Its contexts include blood, death, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דָּגָה (H1710).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: דָּגָה (dâgâh) / H1710 is traced through Genesis 1:26, Genesis 1:28, Exodus 7:18, Exodus 7:21 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: God said, “Let’s make man in our image, after our likeness. Let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over the livestock, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”

God blessed them. God said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and subdue it. Have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the sky, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”
The fish that are in the river will die and the river will become foul. The Egyptians will loathe to drink water from the river.” ’ ”
The fish that were in the river died. The river became foul. The Egyptians couldn’t drink water from the river. The blood was throughout all the land of Egypt.
We remember the fish, which we ate in Egypt for nothing; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic;
the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the water under the earth;
He turned their waters into blood,
Why, when I came, was there no one?
I will put hooks in your jaws,
I will put hooks in your jaws,
I’ll cast you out into the wilderness,

It will happen, that every living creature which swarms, in every place where the rivers come, will live. Then there will be a very great multitude of fish; for these waters have come there, and the waters of the sea will be healed, and everything will live wherever the river comes.

It will happen, that fishermen will stand by it. From En Gedi even to En Eglaim will be a place for the spreading of nets. Their fish will be after their kinds, as the fish of the great sea, exceedingly many.

definitions.full: H1710. dagah דָּגָה noun feminine fish (Late Hebrew id. ) — דָּגָה Num 11:5 5 t.; construct דְּגַת Gen 1:26 4 t. + Ezek 29:4 b (strike out B Co); suffix דְּגָתוֺ 47:10 ᵑ9 ᵐ5 Co; ( דגתם ᵑ0 ), דְּגָתָם Isa 50:2 ; Psa 105:29 + Ezek 47:10 ᵑ0 compare above — fish , almost always collective; fish of sea הַיָּם דְּגַת Gen 1:26 , 28 (P) Ezek 47:10 (in simile); in Nile ( יְאֹר ) Exod 7:18 , 21 (E) compare Psa 105:29 , יְאֹרֶיךָ דְּגַת Ezek 29:4 (twice in verse) (compare above) 29:5 ; in sea and rivers Isa 50:2 ; Ezek 47:9-10 , food in Egypt Num 11:5 (JE); image of fish forbidden in worship, as of beasts and birds Deut 4:18 (on sacredness of fish, and use in sacrifice compare Selden De Diis Syris, ii. 3. RS Sern. i. 274 ); of single fish only Jonah 2:2 ( 2:1 (twice in verse); Jonah 2:11 דָּג ) by late usage; compare conversely דָּאג = דָּגָה collective Neh 13:16 .
definitions.rootNote: feminine of 1709 , and meaning the same
